newsitem.title: UKRAINE: World Bank could commit $1 bln to Ukraine in 1997.
newsitem.headline: World Bank could commit $1 bln to Ukraine in 1997.

text.p: A World Bank managing director said on Thursday the bank could give Ukraine up to $1 billion this year if it quickly passed the 1997 budget and a package of tax reforms to underpin it.
"If we have the budget passed and all the other legislation, with best efforts we could disperse up to $1 billion this year," Caio Koch-Weser said at a news conference.
"But this is the very best scenario because there is a lot of work still lying ahead for both sides to accomplish that," he added.

Koch-Weser met President Leonid Kuchma, Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko and Roman Shpek, head of the National Agency for Reconstruction and Development, during his week-long visit to Ukraine.
Parliament is expected to review and pass the budget, which was due on January 1 sometime next month.

The World Bank has committed $2 billion for 12 projects in the areas of energy, environmental preservation and government and economic reform, Koch-Weser said. The budget would pave the way for Ukraine's receipt of a $2.5 to $3 billion credit from the International Monetary Fund.
